name: 2 Samuel

overview.author: Not stated. Likely compiled from records by Nathan, Gad, and others (1 Chronicles 29:29). Originally one book with 1 Samuel.
overview.date: The events cover David’s reign, about 1010–970 BC. It was compiled after the kingdom divided (around 930 BC) or later.
overview.audience: Israel under the kings, and later the exiles, who needed to remember God’s covenant with David and its promise of an eternal throne.
overview.setting: Hebron and then Jerusalem, which David captures and makes his capital, along with the surrounding nations he subdues.
overview.purpose: To show how God established David’s kingdom, made an everlasting covenant with his house, and remained faithful even when David sinned terribly and suffered the consequences.
overview.structure: David’s triumphs (1–10), David’s sin with Bathsheba (11–12), David’s troubles (13–20), and an appendix of reflections on his reign (21–24).

items.title: King over Judah, then all Israel

themes.title: The Davidic Covenant
themes.text: God promises David an everlasting house, kingdom, and throne (7:12–16), the foundation of messianic hope.

themes.title: Sin and Consequences
themes.text: David’s adultery and murder are forgiven, but “the sword shall never depart from your house” (12:10).

themes.title: Repentance and Grace
themes.text: David’s honest confession (“I have sinned against the LORD”) brings forgiveness (12:13; Psalm 51).

themes.title: Kindness (Hesed)
themes.text: David shows covenant kindness to Mephibosheth for Jonathan’s sake (ch. 9).

themes.title: God’s Sovereignty in Politics
themes.text: Through intrigue and rebellion, God establishes and preserves David’s throne.

themes.title: Worship
themes.text: David dances before the ark and insists on offerings that cost him something (6; 24).

christInBook.text: The promise of an eternal Son of David is fulfilled in Jesus (Luke 1:32–33; Acts 2:29–36).
“I will be to him a father, and he shall be to me a son” is applied to Christ (Hebrews 1:5).
Jerusalem becomes the city of David, where the Son of David will die and rise.
David’s kindness to lame Mephibosheth, seated at the king’s table, pictures grace to sinners in Christ.
David weeping as he crosses the Kidron and climbs the Mount of Olives foreshadows Jesus’ path on the night of His betrayal (John 18:1).

crossReferences.note: Reflections on the covenant with David.
Jesus given the throne of His father David.
God raised up David, and from his offspring a Savior.
Jesus the son of David; “the wife of Uriah.”

reflection: David’s fall began when he stayed home and kept looking (11:1–2). What situations make you most vulnerable to temptation?
Nathan told David the truth with wisdom. Who in your life has permission to say, “You are the man”?
David invited Mephibosheth to his table for Jonathan’s sake. Whom could you show kindness to for Christ’s sake?
How does God’s covenant promise to David strengthen your confidence in His promises to you in Christ?
David refused to give God offerings that cost him nothing. What does costly devotion look like for you?

chapterList.title: David Mourns Saul and Jonathan
chapterList.summary: An Amalekite brings David Saul’s crown, claiming to have killed him and hoping for a reward. David has him executed for striking the LORD’s anointed. Then David laments Saul and Jonathan in a moving song: “How the mighty have fallen!”
questions: Why does David mourn Saul, his enemy?
What does David’s lament reveal about his love for Jonathan?
How can we grieve honestly, even over complicated relationships?

chapterList.title: David King over Judah; Civil War
chapterList.summary: David inquires of the LORD and goes to Hebron, where Judah anoints him king. Abner makes Saul’s son Ish-bosheth king over Israel. War breaks out, and Abner reluctantly kills Joab’s brother Asahel.
questions: How does David seek God before acting (2:1)?
How does David honor the men of Jabesh-gilead?
What does the Asahel incident reveal about the cost of conflict?

chapterList.title: Abner Joins David; Joab Kills Abner
chapterList.summary: David’s house grows stronger. Abner quarrels with Ish-bosheth and offers to bring Israel to David. Joab, avenging his brother, treacherously murders Abner. David publicly mourns and distances himself from the crime.
questions: How does God move hearts to bring the kingdom to David?
Why does David publicly mourn Abner?
What does David mean by “these men... are more severe than I” (3:39)?

chapterList.title: Ish-bosheth Murdered
chapterList.summary: Two captains assassinate Ish-bosheth and bring his head to David, expecting reward. David executes them for murdering an innocent man in his own bed. Jonathan’s lame son Mephibosheth is introduced.
questions: Why does David refuse to benefit from treachery?
How does David trust God to give him the throne in God’s way?
Why might Mephibosheth be mentioned here?

chapterList.title: David King over All Israel; Jerusalem Captured
chapterList.summary: All Israel anoints David king at Hebron. David captures Jerusalem, the Jebusite stronghold, and makes it the City of David. He grows greater because the LORD was with him, and he defeats the Philistines after inquiring of the LORD.
questions: Why does David perceive that God established him “for the sake of his people Israel” (5:12)?
Why is Jerusalem so important in the rest of Scripture?
How does David seek God’s guidance differently in each battle?

chapterList.title: The Ark Brought to Jerusalem
chapterList.summary: David moves the ark on a new cart, and when Uzzah touches it, he dies. Afraid, David leaves the ark with Obed-edom, whose house is blessed. Later David brings it to Jerusalem properly, dancing before the LORD with all his might. Michal despises him.
questions: Why was Uzzah’s touch so serious (see Numbers 4:15)?
What can we learn from David’s uninhibited worship?
How does David respond to Michal’s criticism (6:21–22)?

chapterList.title: God’s Covenant with David
chapterList.summary: David wants to build a house for God. Through Nathan, God says instead that He will build David a “house,” a dynasty: David’s offspring will build the temple, and his throne will be established forever. David responds with humble, wondering prayer: “Who am I, O Lord GOD?”
questions: What specific promises does God make in 7:8–16?
How are these promises fulfilled in Jesus?
What do you learn from David’s response in prayer (7:18–29)?

chapterList.title: David’s Victories
chapterList.summary: David defeats the Philistines, Moab, Zobah, Syria, and Edom. “The LORD gave victory to David wherever he went.” He dedicates the plunder to God and administers justice and equity to all his people.
questions: What phrase repeats in this chapter (8:6, 14)?
How does David use wealth from victory?
What does good government look like (8:15)?

chapterList.title: David and Mephibosheth
chapterList.summary: David asks, “Is there still anyone left of the house of Saul, that I may show him kindness for Jonathan’s sake?” He finds Mephibosheth, lame in both feet, restores his family land, and has him eat at the king’s table like one of his sons.
questions: Why might Mephibosheth have feared David?
How does this story picture the gospel?
Who could you show “the kindness of God” to (9:3)?

chapterList.title: Victory over Ammon and Syria
chapterList.summary: David sends condolences to the new Ammonite king, who humiliates his envoys. War follows, and Joab defeats the Ammonites and Syrians. Joab says, “Be of good courage... and may the LORD do what seems good to him.”
questions: How did a misunderstanding lead to war?
What do you admire about Joab’s words in 10:12?
How can we act courageously while leaving results to God?

chapterList.title: David and Bathsheba
chapterList.summary: In spring, when kings go to war, David stays in Jerusalem. He sees Bathsheba bathing, takes her, and she becomes pregnant. David tries to cover it up by bringing Uriah home, and when that fails he arranges Uriah’s death in battle. “The thing that David had done displeased the LORD.”
questions: Trace David’s steps into sin. Where could he have stopped?
How does Uriah’s integrity contrast with David’s?
Why does sin often lead to more sin to cover it up?

chapterList.title: Nathan Rebukes David
chapterList.summary: Nathan tells a parable of a rich man who stole a poor man’s only lamb. David is furious, and Nathan says, “You are the man!” David confesses, “I have sinned against the LORD,” and is forgiven, but the child dies and violence will plague his house. Solomon is later born and loved by God.
questions: Why was a parable an effective way to confront David?
How does David respond to the death of the child (12:20–23)?
Read Psalm 51. What does it add to this story?

chapterList.title: Amnon and Tamar; Absalom’s Revenge
chapterList.summary: David’s son Amnon rapes his half-sister Tamar. David is angry but does nothing. Two years later Absalom, Tamar’s brother, murders Amnon and flees.
questions: How does David’s passivity contribute to the tragedy?
How do the consequences of David’s sin (12:10–11) begin to unfold?
How should families and churches respond to abuse?

chapterList.title: Absalom Returns
chapterList.summary: Joab uses a wise woman from Tekoa to persuade David to bring Absalom home. David allows it but refuses to see him for two years. Absalom forces Joab’s hand by burning his field, and David finally receives him with a kiss.
questions: What principle does the woman state in 14:14?
What was missing in David’s half-reconciliation with Absalom?
How does true reconciliation differ from just avoiding conflict?

chapterList.title: Absalom’s Conspiracy
chapterList.summary: Absalom steals the hearts of Israel by flattering people at the city gate, then declares himself king in Hebron. David flees Jerusalem weeping, sending the ark back and trusting God: “Let him do to me what seems good to him.” Loyal friends like Ittai and Hushai stand with him.
questions: How did Absalom “steal the hearts” of the people?
What do you admire about David’s attitude in 15:25–26?
What can we learn from Ittai’s loyalty (15:21)?

chapterList.title: Ziba and Shimei
chapterList.summary: Ziba brings supplies and slanders Mephibosheth. Shimei curses and throws stones at David, but David refuses to retaliate: “Leave him alone... It may be that the LORD will look on the wrong done to me.” Absalom follows Ahithophel’s advice to take David’s concubines publicly.
questions: How does David respond to Shimei’s cursing?
How is 16:22 a fulfillment of Nathan’s prophecy (12:11)?
How do you respond when you are insulted?

chapterList.title: Hushai Defeats Ahithophel’s Counsel
chapterList.summary: Ahithophel advises an immediate attack on David, but Hushai, David’s friend, persuades Absalom to wait. “For the LORD had ordained to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel.” David is warned and crosses the Jordan. Ahithophel hangs himself.
questions: How does God answer David’s prayer in 15:31?
How does God work through ordinary human advice?
What does Ahithophel’s end show?

chapterList.title: Absalom’s Death
chapterList.summary: David’s army defeats Absalom’s forces in the forest of Ephraim. Absalom’s head catches in an oak, and Joab kills him against David’s order. David weeps: “O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! Would I had died instead of you.”
questions: What does David’s grief reveal about a father’s love?
Why do you think Joab disobeyed David?
How does David’s cry point to the heart of God for rebellious children?

chapterList.title: David Returns to Jerusalem
chapterList.summary: Joab rebukes David for mourning while his loyal men feel ashamed. David returns to Jerusalem, pardons Shimei, hears Mephibosheth’s side, and honors old Barzillai. Tension rises between Judah and Israel.
questions: Why was Joab’s rebuke necessary, even if harsh?
How does David show mercy on his return?
What do you learn from Mephibosheth’s response (19:30)?

chapterList.title: Sheba’s Rebellion
chapterList.summary: Sheba leads Israel in revolt. Joab murders Amasa, David’s new commander, and pursues Sheba to Abel. A wise woman negotiates with Joab, and the city throws Sheba’s head over the wall, ending the revolt.
questions: How does the wise woman save her city?
What does Joab’s violence reveal about the dangers in David’s court?
How can one wise voice prevent disaster?

chapterList.title: The Gibeonites Avenged; Philistine Giants
chapterList.summary: A three-year famine comes because of Saul’s violation of Israel’s treaty with the Gibeonites. David makes amends, and Rizpah keeps vigil over her sons’ bodies. David’s mighty men defeat four Philistine giants.
questions: Why does God take broken oaths so seriously (Joshua 9)?
What do you learn from Rizpah’s devotion?
Why does David’s men’s request (21:17) show his value to Israel?

chapterList.title: David’s Song of Deliverance
chapterList.summary: David sings a song of praise to God for deliverance from all his enemies and from Saul: “The LORD is my rock and my fortress and my deliverer.” He describes God thundering from heaven to rescue him and declares, “This God, his way is perfect.”
questions: Which image of God in this song speaks most to you?
What does David mean by “he rescued me, because he delighted in me” (22:20)?
This song is also Psalm 18. Why might it appear in both places?

chapterList.title: David’s Last Words; Mighty Men
chapterList.summary: David’s last words describe the righteous ruler who is like the morning sun and the everlasting covenant God made with him. A list honors David’s mighty men, including three who broke through enemy lines to bring him water, which he poured out to the LORD.
questions: How does 23:3–4 describe the ideal ruler, and who fulfills it?
Why did David pour out the water rather than drink it (23:15–17)?
Who are the “mighty men” who have served faithfully alongside you?

chapterList.title: The Census and the Altar
chapterList.summary: David orders a census of the fighting men, an act of pride, and is conscience-stricken. God sends a plague, and 70,000 die. David pleads for the people, and Gad tells him to build an altar on Araunah’s threshing floor. David insists on paying: “I will not offer... offerings that cost me nothing.” The plague stops.
questions: Why was the census sinful?
What does David’s intercession (24:17) show about his heart?
This site later became the temple (2 Chronicles 3:1). What is the significance?

tagline: David’s reign: covenant blessing, grievous sin, and lasting grace
readingPlan: 24 chapters: one chapter a day takes 24 days; two a day takes about 12 days. For each chapter, read it on ESV.org, then come back here for the summary, questions, and your notes.
